Here is how blocking works:

  • A blocked subverse will be removed from /v/all (after cache has updated; give it ten minutes)
  • A subverse cannot be removed from the front page by blocking

The front page can take one of two forms:

  • A list of subverses to which a user has subscribed
  • The /s/Default set, if the user has not subscribed to any subverses

If the user has subscribed to subverses, and wants /v/aww to be removed from the front page specifically (https://voat.co/ rather than https://voat.co/v/all), the way to do this is simply to make sure the user is not subscribed to /v/aww. Blocking the subverse is insufficient; you must ensure you are not subscribed to it, because a subverse subscription will always override a subverse block.

If the user has not subscribed to any subverses, it is not possible to remove /v/aww from the front page.

This is because, by not subscribing to any subverses, you automatically subscribe to /s/Default, which includes /v/aww. Because subscriptions override blocks, you effectively are subscribed to /v/aww without having subscribed to any subverses, and therefore it cannot be removed frmo your front page. However, if you have /v/aww blocked, viewing /v/all will give you a feed with every subverse on Voat, except for /v/aww (and whatever other subverses you have blocked).

So, if you ever find that you have blocked a subverse but it isn't disappearing from your feed, consider a few things:

  • Have you waited ten minutes? It takes a few minutes for Voat's cache to update and for your subscription / blocking to "take effect".
  • Are you subscribed to the subverse you are trying to block, either directly or via a set? If so, blocking it will not remove it from your front page. If your priority is to remove a subverse from your front page specifically, your focus should not be on blocking the subverse, but on making sure you are not subscribed to it in some way.
